Yes, the demand was too high on 16 June.

The plant's contract capacity is 1250 kW [data: get_plant_overview]. On 16 June, the peak demand reached 1324.4 kW at 08:15, exceeding the contract by 74.4 kW (6% over) [data: get_demand]. There were 2 intervals where the demand was above the contract:
- 08:00: 1307.1 kW
- 08:15: 1324.4 kW

This incident corresponds to scenario S2, "Monday morning simultaneous start," which occurred from 06:00 to 11:00 on that day [data: get_plant_overview].

The documents state that reflow ovens must be switched off rather than left in standby over the weekend because a reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating (25.2 kW) continuously, whereas a properly switched-off oven uses only about 340-350 kWh per oven-weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), reflow oven RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. The weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh against the normal 346 kWh, resulting in an excess of about 1,210 kWh from that single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

According to the demand-exceedance procedure:

**First load shed:** EV charging (EV-01) is paused first, shedding 100% of its present load [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]. This is because it has no effect on production [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].

**Loads that must never be shed:**
- Server room (DC-01) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
